description: Wire scope-exclusion SUPPRESSION into the V8 engine so scope-excluded scenarios are DROPPED in BOTH default (grounded-only) and analyst modes, on BOTH the main and narrow-CR paths. Uses modules/scope_exclusion.py (FEAT-002). Drops are logged per-TC and summarized on suite.warnings (visible in the Summary sheet). Reconciles with the Chalk-first coverage invariant so an intentionally-excluded Chalk scenario does not trigger a false coverage warning. Default output for features WITHOUT exclusion language stays byte-identical (the pass is a no-op when the excluded set is empty). Depends on FEAT-002.
steps: In modules/data_first_engine.py add _apply_scope_exclusion(suite, jira, chalk, log) modelled on _prune_degenerate_tcs (line 1306): excluded = scope_exclusion.extract_excluded_subjects(jira, chalk, log); if not excluded: return (no-op). Else iterate suite.test_cases, keep non-matching, skip tc.user_requested (never drop user-requested), and for each match call log('[SCOPE] dropped TC '%s' — excluded by comment: '%s'' % (title, phrase)). After the loop, if any dropped, set suite.test_cases = kept and append ONE summary line to suite.warnings, e.g. '[SCOPE] Dropped N test case(s) excluded by scope language: <phrases>'. Return the set of dropped TC titles/traceability for the coverage reconciliation step.

Call _apply_scope_exclusion on the MAIN path AFTER StepAssembler.reconcile and tc_name_polish/api_step_grounder and BEFORE the final _assert_chalk_coverage (around line 830, just before the RULE #1 invariant block). Call it on the CR path (_build_cr_suite_v8) before its final _assert_chalk_coverage (around line 1225-1230). Both modes run it (do NOT gate on data_only).

Reconcile with _assert_chalk_coverage (line 909): a dropped TC may be the only cover for a scope-excluded Chalk scenario. Make the coverage check NOT warn for intentionally-excluded scenarios — simplest: pass the excluded-subject set (or the dropped-scenario provenance) into _assert_chalk_coverage and skip any Chalk scenario whose title matches an excluded subject via scope_exclusion.scenario_matches_excluded. Keep the existing provenance/substring matching otherwise unchanged.

In modules/analyst_validity.py, make scenario_is_valid aware of scope exclusion so analyst scenarios matching an excluded subject are dropped before reconcile. Thread the excluded set into apply_analyst_validity_gate (compute it once via scope_exclusion.extract_excluded_subjects(jira, chalk) at the top of the gate, next to build_feature_evidence) and, for each analyst TC, if scenario_matches_excluded(tc, excluded) -> treat as 'drop' (log with the same [SCOPE] message) BEFORE the existing kind-based verdict. Grounded TCs are still handled by the new engine pass; keep the gate's grounded-always-keep behavior intact otherwise.
Ensure determinism: iterate in existing list order, no set-ordering leakage into output (sort any phrase list used in log/warning text).
acceptance_criteria: In default mode, a feature whose evidence says 'scope excluded for cross-environment fan-out' has its cross-env/multi-environment/fan-out TCs dropped; an in-scope 'file pickup' TC is kept.
A feature with NO exclusion language produces a byte-identical suite vs before this feature (tests/test_analyst_mode_regression.py and tests/test_suite_snapshot.py pass unchanged).
Each dropped TC emits a '[SCOPE] dropped TC ... — excluded by comment: ...' log line and suite.warnings gains one summary line that renders on the Summary sheet.
_assert_chalk_coverage does not emit a coverage warning for a scenario that was intentionally scope-excluded.
Suppression applies in analyst mode too (apply_analyst_validity_gate drops matching analyst TCs).
verification: python -m pytest tests/test_scope_exclusion.py tests/test_analyst_mode_regression.py tests/test_suite_snapshot.py tests/test_analyst_validity_gate.py -q
python -m pytest -q   (full suite stays green; no byte-identicality regressions)
findings:
IMPLEMENTED (option A, per parent decision — conservative-distinctive guard; FEAT-002 extractor left untouched).

What was wired:
- modules/data_first_engine.py: added _apply_scope_exclusion(suite, jira, chalk, log) modeled on _prune_degenerate_tcs — no-op when extract_excluded_subjects returns empty (byte-identical default output preserved), never drops user_requested TCs, prefers DROP, logs each drop as "[SCOPE] dropped TC '<title>' — excluded by comment: '<phrase>'", and appends ONE deterministic suite.warnings summary line (phrases sorted). Called on the MAIN path (@~833, after reconcile/tc_name_polish/api_step_grounder, before the RULE #1 _assert_chalk_coverage) AND the CR path _build_cr_suite_v8 (@~1305, before its _assert_chalk_coverage). Both run regardless of data_only (default AND analyst).
- _assert_chalk_coverage now takes excluded_subjects=None and skips an intentionally scope-excluded Chalk scenario (via scope_exclusion.scenario_matches_excluded + the distinctive guard) from BOTH the covered numerator and the total denominator, so an intentional exclusion never raises a false RULE #1 coverage warning.
- modules/analyst_validity.py: apply_analyst_validity_gate computes the excluded set once (scope_exclusion.extract_excluded_subjects) next to build_feature_evidence and drops matching analyst TCs (prefer DROP, same [SCOPE] log) BEFORE the kind-based verdict; grounded-always-keep behaviour intact.

CONSERVATIVE GUARD (_scope_phrase_is_distinctive, mirrored in both modules): a matched phrase only triggers a DROP when it is DISTINCTIVE — a hyphen compound (fan-out, cross-environment, multi-environment), the bounded cross-env/across-environments family, or a phrase of >=3 words. A generic 2-word fragment NEVER drops. This is the fix for the do-no-harm problem: FEAT-002's _expand_variants splits 'Verizon/CBRS billing-record ... out of scope' into the generic 'billing record', which without the guard matched and ZEROED 4628's 9 in-scope TMO billing TCs. Accepted trade-off (per parent): 4628's vaguely-worded exclusion now drops NOTHING (stays at full count), including its one Verizon/CBRS TC — under-dropping a vague exclusion is acceptable; over-dropping in-scope TCs is not.
